author: delegate-gp[bot]
title: ENG-11619 Count only front-end exceptions raised from code we ship
body:
**Why.** The *New front-end error in prod* rule (`frontend-error-new`, rule uid `eg3jdgetntse8f`) fired at 2026-11-11T03:41:10Z on `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'window.ethereum.selectedAddress = undefined')`. That code is not ours — `git grep -niI ethereum origin/main` finds nothing — and the 12 events are one Brave 27.2.1 / iOS 18.7 session in which the wallet injector throws in page context, so Faro frames it at `https://app.goodparty.org/dashboard:1:16`.

The rule was supposed to drop it. Its noise filter dropped a `chrome-extension://` frame, which only exists when an injector runs in its own origin; an iOS wallet injector is a `WKUserScript` running in the page's context, so the browser has no script URL to report and frames it at the document. Measured on the stream instead of assumed, over the week to 2026-11-11: 85 exception lines, **zero** with an extension-scheme frame, and the two largest noise groups (redacted `Script error.` 27, Google Tag Manager's `gtag` failing to load 27) pass that filter as well. The filter never matched the noise it was written for.

**What changes.** The denylist becomes attribution. `EXTENSION_FRAMES` is replaced by `SHIPPED_CODE_FRAMES`: an exception is counted only when its line carries a frame at `/_next/static/…` (a chunk we built) or `turbopack:///…` (the path Faro source-maps it to). The extension regex is deleted, not widened. Both rules keep their shape, thresholds and read budget; the fetch-wording denylist stays, because a failed fetch raised by our own code is ours and still unactionable. `docs/observability.md` § Front-end errors now states the predicate, what it drops and what it costs.

**Removes the root cause; it does not mitigate it.** The root cause is that the rule decided what to page on by enumerating what is not ours, so an in-page injector passed every filter by construction, and every browser or extension release adds a shape the list has never seen. After this change there is no list to extend: the predicate is a property of the build we shipped, and everything that fails it is not a bug we can fix. The five whys on the ticket: [ENG-11619 comment](https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2bexjj?comment=1400430000333816).

**Evidence.** Loki `grafanacloud-logs`, read-only, bounded:

- The hour that fired (`{service_name="gp-webapp-prod", kind="exception"}`, 02:45Z–03:45Z) with the new filter: **0** lines, against 12 for the old one.
- The week 2026-11-04→11-11: **85 → 9** lines counted. The 9 are `Minified React error #418` ×6 (hydration mismatch), the `useTrackerTasks` `e.some is not a function` TypeError ×1, and two chat-attachment `presign` 400s. Dropped: 27 `Script error.`, 27 `gtag`, 12 this TypeError, 4 `network error` and 2 `presign` 400s with no frame in our build, 4 network wordings.
- Trade-off, documented in the code and the doc: an error thrown by inline script in our own HTML has no chunk frame and is dropped with the noise. None in the week above; gp-webapp's app code is all chunks.
- The same TypeError will return with the next Brave release and the next injected global. It is now invisible without naming Brave in the rule.

**Checks.** `frontend-error-alerts.test.ts` gains the rule-level assertion and the frame cases (in-page injector, redacted cross-origin error, extension scheme, third-party runtime, chunk and turbopack frames). All six alerting suites pass (219 tests) and `npx tsc -p tsconfig.deploy.json` is clean. Note: this worker has no Docker, so the alerting suites ran under a temporary vitest config with the Postgres global setup disabled; that config is not committed, and the alerting files touch no database.

Risk: low — an alert-rule definition, its tests and docs. No runtime, auth, data or deploy path changes.

Recent work in this area: @swain #3696

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Alert rule and test/doc changes only; no runtime, auth, or deploy paths touched.
> 
> **Overview**
> Front-end error alerts (`frontend-error-spreading`, `frontend-error-new`) no longer rely on a `chrome-extension://` denylist. They now **require** a stack line matching **`SHIPPED_CODE_FRAMES`** (`/_next/static/` or `turbopack:///`) so only exceptions attributable to the built app are grouped and paged.
> 
> Network-failure message filtering is unchanged. Alert copy and **docs/observability.md** describe what gets dropped (in-page injectors, `Script error.`, third-party tag runtimes, empty stacks) and the trade-off that inline HTML errors without chunk frames are ignored. Tests assert the LogQL filter on both rules and cover keep/drop frame examples, including the Brave wallet injector case.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fbcfa3c9a80063a4db9fd0270d32a4a41317224a. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

@@ -237,8 +237,25 @@ E2E or QA test user is signed in.

   `error_type` and `error_message`, which is what a ticket is deduplicated
-  on. Both rules drop network failures (`Failed to fetch`, `Load failed` and
-  the like) and errors thrown from browser-extension frames.
+  on. Both rules also drop network failures (`Failed to fetch`, `Load failed`
+  and the like), and — the filter that does most of the work — they count only
+  an exception with a stack frame in the bundle we shipped: a frame at
+  `/_next/static/…`, or at the `turbopack:///…` path Faro source-maps it to.
+
+  That one condition is why a browser-injected script cannot page a human. A
+  script the browser or an extension injects runs in the page's own context,
+  so its frame is the DOCUMENT URL with a synthetic line and column, not
+  `chrome-extension://`: on 2026-11-11 Brave's wallet injector on iOS threw
+  `window.ethereum.selectedAddress = undefined` 12 times in one session and
+  every event framed at `https://app.goodparty.org/dashboard:1:16`. The same
+  filter drops the redacted `Script error.` a cross-origin script produces, a
+  third-party tag runtime (Google Tag Manager's `gtag` failing to load), and
+  an exception with no stack at all. In the 7 days to 2026-11-11 those were 76
+  of the stream's 85 exception lines — 72 with no frame in our build and 4
+  network failures — so the 9 that reached a group were real app errors.
+
+  The cost: an error thrown by inline script in our own HTML has no chunk
+  frame and is dropped with them. gp-webapp's app code is all chunks.
 
 ## Debugging an incident with the MCPs

@@ -40,20 +42,54 @@ export const NETWORK_FAILURE_MESSAGES =
   '^(failed to fetch|load failed|networkerror when attempting to fetch resource\\.?|network request failed)( \\(.*\\))?$'
 
 /**
- * A stack frame from a browser extension: an error thrown by code we do not
- * ship, on a page it injected itself into.
+ * A stack frame from code we ship: a frame the browser points at one of our
+ * built chunks (`/_next/static/…`), or at the source-mapped path Faro
+ * resolves it to (`turbopack:///…`, the Next 16 build).
+ *
+ * THIS IS A POSITIVE FILTER, and that is the point. A rule can carry a list
+ * of things that are not ours — an extension scheme, a fetch wording, a tag
+ * runtime — and that list has no end: every browser release and every
+ * extension adds one, and each one pages a human until somebody widens the
+ * list. "A frame in the build we just shipped" is instead a property we can
+ * test, and everything that fails it is by definition not a bug we can fix.
+ * What fails it:

+ * - a script injected into the page by the browser or an extension. It runs
+ *   in the page's own context, so its frame is the DOCUMENT URL with a
+ *   synthetic line and column (`at global code (https://app.goodparty.org/
+ *   dashboard:1:16)`), not `chrome-extension://`. Brave's wallet injector on
+ *   iOS did exactly that 12 times in one session on 2026-11-11, and every one
+ *   of them looked like a new error in our own code.
+ * - a cross-origin script error, which browsers redact to `Script error.`
+ *   with a single `:0:0` frame on the document URL. 27 of the 85 lines in the
+ *   week to 2026-11-11.
+ * - a third-party tag runtime loaded by our analytics snippet, which frames at
+ *   its own bundle (27 of the 85: Google Tag Manager's `gtag` failing to
+ *   load).
+ * - an exception Faro recorded with no stack at all, which has no frame for a
+ *   reader to act on anyway.
+ *
+ * The cost: an error thrown by inline script in our own HTML has no chunk
+ * frame and is dropped with them. Nothing in the stream above came from
+ * inline code, and gp-webapp's app code is all chunks.
+ *
+ * RE2 syntax, sent inside the double-quoted LogQL string below. It is a line
+ * filter, so it searches the whole line rather than matching the parsed
+ * `stacktrace` value whole — which also keeps a chunk-load failure whose
+ * MESSAGE names an `/_next/static/` URL while its stack does not, the safe
+ * direction to be wrong in.
  */

+export const SHIPPED_CODE_FRAMES = 'turbopack:///|/_next/static/'

- * The extension filter is a line filter, applied before parsing, because the
- * frame can sit anywhere in the stack trace.
+ * The frame filter is a line filter, applied before parsing, because the frame
+ * can sit anywhere in the stack trace.

   [
     '{service_name="gp-webapp-$ENV", kind="exception"}',
-    `!~ "${EXTENSION_FRAMES}"`,
+    `|~ "${SHIPPED_CODE_FRAMES}"`,
     '| logfmt app_environment, type, value, session_id',
     '| app_environment = "$ENV"',
     `| value !~ \`(?i)${NETWORK_FAILURE_MESSAGES}\``,
